readiness.hed: Fredericksburg stays cloudy and cool today near 54 before rain moves in tonight ahead of a windy, rain-soaked Thanksgiving Day under an active Wind Advisory, with lingering showers Thursday night and a drier, breezier Friday near 57 before Friday night clears to partly cloudy near 38
readiness.insight: The National Weather Service has a Wind Advisory in effect for Fredericksburg and the surrounding region from 1 a.m. to 1 p.m. EST Thursday — Thanksgiving Day itself — for northeast winds of 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 to 55 mph, enough to blow around unsecured objects, down tree limbs and cause scattered power outages. Today stays cloudy and seasonably cool with a high near 54 and light northeast wind, but rain moves in after 8 p.m. tonight, with a 100 percent chance of precipitation overnight and 1 to 2 inches of rain possible by morning. That system continues straight into Thanksgiving Day, with NWS calling for a high near 59, a 100 percent chance of rain, gusts to 45 mph and another 2 to 3 inches of rainfall — the wettest, windiest day of the stretch — before Thursday night tapers to a 40 percent chance of lingering light rain near 45. Friday turns drier and breezier, with a slight morning rain chance giving way to partial sun and a high near 57, before Friday night clears out to partly cloudy skies near 38.
actions: The Wind Advisory runs 1 a.m. to 1 p.m. Thursday — secure trash cans, decorations and anything loose outside before Thanksgiving dinner prep begins.
Heavy rain (1-2 inches) arrives tonight and continues into Thursday — if you're hosting, move outdoor seating, games or any turkey-fryer setup under cover now.
Gusts to 45-55 mph combined with soaked ground raise the odds of downed limbs and power flickers Thursday — charge devices and have a flashlight ready before bed tonight.
If you're driving to Thanksgiving dinner Thursday morning, build in extra time for high wind and standing water on the roads, especially in a high-profile vehicle.
